title: Compute-Optimal Safety Reasoning via Dynamic Token Allocation
summary: This paper re-examines the trade-off between model scale and inference-time compute for safety alignment. It proposes dynamically allocating tokens between safety reasoning and task completion during generation, using a lightweight router model. Unlike fixed compute scaling, this method adapts token budgets per query, prioritizing safety checks for high-risk prompts. Evaluated on ShieldGemma and HarmBench, it achieves better safety-performance trade-offs than static scaling methods.
gap: Prior work assumes fixed compute budgets for inference-time alignment, but safety-critical queries may require disproportionate compute. Existing methods like Best-of-N or test-time scaling treat all prompts equally, ignoring risk variability.
approach: Train a lightweight router model to predict the optimal token split between safety reasoning (e.g., guideline verification) and task execution. During generation, the router allocates tokens dynamically: high-risk prompts trigger extended safety checks, while low-risk prompts allocate more tokens to task completion. The router is trained on a combination of ShieldGemma safety labels and compute-cost data.
evaluation: Baselines include fixed Best-of-N, static compute scaling, and Llama Guard. Metrics are safety score (ShieldGemma benchmarks), task performance (e.g., question answering accuracy), and compute efficiency (FLOPs per query). The evaluation uses a mixed dataset of harmless and harmful prompts from HarmBench and Advbench.
